title: Neighborhood Missions: path to a production-quality title
qualityClaim: Stylized browser-game vertical slice. AAA-quality ambition, not AAA certification.

statusDefinitions.verified: A narrow acceptance criterion has recorded automated evidence; not human art approval or physical hardware certification.
statusDefinitions.implemented: Code is integrated; specific acceptance or release evidence remains to be recorded.
statusDefinitions.partial: A baseline exists, but the full production criterion is not met.
statusDefinitions.needs-playtest: Requires real hardware or human evaluation; automated tests cannot substitute.
statusDefinitions.blocked: Cannot pass until prerequisites and approvals are complete.

milestones.title: Stop fighting the game
milestones.exitCriterion: Measured control, save and performance baseline.
milestones.humanGate: Approve a 10-minute high-speed route on a named desktop and physical Xbox controller.

milestones.title: One exceptional neighborhood
milestones.exitCriterion: A coherent Homecoming vertical slice before more map expansion.
milestones.humanGate: Approve one street, hero character, vehicle, interior and a compelling 15-minute play experience.

milestones.title: A city with a reason to exist
milestones.exitCriterion: Distinct districts, useful buildings and believable activity.
milestones.humanGate: Explore without relying on repeated delivery templates or empty distance.

milestones.title: A campaign worth finishing
milestones.exitCriterion: Authored missions, progression, consequences and replay depth.
milestones.humanGate: Fresh players can describe the story and choose a next activity without coaching.

milestones.title: Production-grade presentation
milestones.exitCriterion: Consistent art, animation, acoustics and accessibility.
milestones.humanGate: Approve actual gameplay reference shots, controller sessions and listening tests.

milestones.title: Release readiness
milestones.exitCriterion: Reliable builds, recovery, licensing and sustained hardware testing.
milestones.humanGate: Pass the named device matrix, license audit, soak test and rollback drill.

items.title: Continuous acceleration and explicit braking
items.acceptance: 90 simulated seconds at full acceleration without energy-induced drops; coasting preserves speed; LT/B/Ctrl stops. This does not certify physical input latency.
items.next: Retest after every physics change.

items.title: Speed-consistent camera and reduced motion
items.acceptance: Camera FOV and chase distance follow actual speed rather than whether RT is held. Reduced motion removes speed effects.
items.next: Run Homecoming acceptance, then request real-device feel approval.

items.title: Correct camera axes and persistent options
items.acceptance: Right looks right and up looks up. Axis inversion, sensitivity, audio sliders and B-to-return exist. Evidence uses standard-mapping emulation, not physical Xbox hardware.
items.next: Held directions now require neutral before navigating new menus. Complete Windows/browser plus physical Xbox USB and Bluetooth sessions.

items.title: Local frame-time report
items.acceptance: A bounded 600-frame window records p95/p99 interval, CPU submission p95, intervals over 50 ms and simulation/wall ratio. Pauses excluded; no automatic upload.
items.next: Capture results on actual target hardware.

items.title: Named desktop 60 fps gate
items.acceptance: Proposed target: 1920x1080 on RTX 2060-class hardware, warmed 10-minute route, mean >=59 fps, p95 <=18 ms, p99 <=25 ms, fewer than 1 percent of intervals over 50 ms. Record CPU, GPU, browser, quality and power mode. These are project targets, not external certification requirements.
items.next: Run a real-machine benchmark and explicitly review the targets; software-rendered results cannot pass this gate.

items.title: Streaming and stable frame pacing
items.acceptance: No uncapped per-frame world construction. A 30-minute multi-district session must reach stable memory and geometry counts. Rendering must not silently run simulation in slow motion.
items.next: Profile chunk creation, GPU uploads, garbage collection and low-power 30 fps pacing.

items.title: Preserve the existing game and save identities
items.acceptance: Original v1 slot and mission IDs remain. Old saves load; contracts, times and finishes round-trip; sibling game storage is not touched.
items.next: Test additive Homecoming fields and interrupted-write recovery.

items.title: Recoverable save transactions
items.acceptance: Maintain a last-known-good backup with schema migrations and clear recovery. Corrupt storage, quota failures and interrupted writes must not silently erase progress.
items.next: Implement transactional backup and import/export with controller-friendly errors.

items.title: Homecoming story journal and named neighbors
items.acceptance: Five local contracts gain authored introductions and debriefs. Old completed contracts count; an unrelated active contract is not replaced without explicit consent.
items.next: Measure actual duration with fresh players and improve the authored flow; 15 minutes remains a target, not a measured result.

items.title: Common Ground changes with your work
items.acceptance: An authored plaza includes Maya, cafe furniture and a pergola. Cleanup removes litter; repairs restore bulbs; photos fill decorative postcard panels; garden/workshop choice changes props. Changes survive reload.
items.next: Automated state transitions passed and actual plaza captures are retained. Human art approval, useful interiors and richer authored assets remain open.

items.title: A physical homecoming finale
items.acceptance: Return to Maya after all five projects. The 500-credit reward and finish unlock are awarded once; remote or repeated claims cannot duplicate rewards.
items.next: Retain exactly-once reward and reload checks in every future release.

items.title: Foreground courier quality
items.acceptance: Approve consistent human scale, face, eyes, hands, clothing, backpack straps and grounded shoes. No visible intersections in standing, running, riding and jumping.
items.next: Replace primitive rig with an original or licensed skinned hero and authored animations.

items.title: Bicycle and unicycle hero assets
items.acceptance: Correct axles, pedals, grips and foot contacts; believable steering, suspension and braking. Approve turntables and riding captures at normal camera distance.
items.next: Build hero meshes, LODs and contact-aware animation.

items.title: Human-scale architecture and materials
items.acceptance: Approve one two-story house, cafe and apartment with believable doors, windows and floor heights. Materials, trim and shadows retain quality across presets.
items.next: Replace enlarged placeholders with measured authored building kits.

items.title: One fully playable interior
items.acceptance: A cafe/workshop needs an accessible entrance, usable counter, collision, a meaningful activity, and a reliable exit with controller, keyboard and touch.
items.next: Validate one interior before repeating it across the city.

items.title: Vertical-slice fun and presentation approval
items.acceptance: At least three fresh-player sessions record confusion, time to first action, exploration and abandonment. The user explicitly approves or rejects the reference-quality street and character.
items.next: Record observations and actual captures rather than self-awarded quality grades.

items.title: Road topology and readable navigation
items.acceptance: All six sphere faces connect. Centerlines, sidewalks, signs and collisions agree. Seams, intersections and mission approaches work at speed.
items.next: Drive every seam and add road-following routes instead of compass-only navigation.

items.title: Distinct coastal districts
items.acceptance: Twenty-four names are not twenty-four distinct experiences. Each district needs a landmark, architecture, terrain or lighting identity, and activity mix.
items.next: Author a downtown, marina, neighborhood and industrial district before scaling further.

items.title: Useful houses and public buildings
items.acceptance: Every building family needs an appropriate encounter or activity; important buildings need interiors. Empty shells remain labeled scenery rather than advertised as interactive homes.
items.next: Create an activity registry, schedules, entrances and usable world markers.

items.title: Traffic that understands streets
items.acceptance: Cars move continuously, but must eventually follow lanes, stop at signals, avoid one another and yield visibly without secretly braking the player.
items.next: Implement intersections, queueing, right of way and safe player interaction.

items.title: Residents with purpose
items.acceptance: Residents, joggers and cyclists exist; add destinations, idles, conversation and crossing behavior rather than only looping around scenery.
items.next: Author bounded schedules, contextual interactions and crowd reactions.

items.title: Parks, rooftops and alternate routes
items.acceptance: Provide street-speed, low-risk sidewalk and stunt/rooftop routes through the slice, each with tested entrances, exits and recovery.
items.next: Prototype short interconnected routes, not isolated scenery.

items.title: Depth rather than mission-count inflation
items.acceptance: The 102 contracts are variants of six systems, not 102 authored stories. New content must add decisions, encounter variation and consequences.
items.next: Deepen one family, playtest it, then expand.

items.title: Connected authored campaign
items.acceptance: Homecoming is the first optional arc. Later chapters need distinct characters, purposeful objectives, debriefs and world consequences.
items.next: Use first-arc feedback to outline two genuinely different follow-up arcs.

items.title: Fair progression and replay
items.acceptance: Credits and cosmetics persist. Duplicate events cannot create repeated rewards. Speed and basic access never require a purchase.
items.next: Balance rewards, add milestone goals and test replay results.

items.title: Navigation that teaches without overwhelming
items.acceptance: A fresh player finds a first task within 60 seconds, follows a road-safe route and distinguishes story, side jobs and free exploration.
items.next: Add local minimap, compact journal and optional route guidance; test with fresh players.

items.title: Difficulty and assistance
items.acceptance: Timing assistance, race recovery, readable scoring and no mandatory repeated-button strain. Assists preserve story access.
items.next: Add persistent steering, timing, objective and retry assists.

items.title: Independent levels and bounded score
items.acceptance: One music transport; independent master, music, effects and ambience; quiet mix and mute; bounded voices. This verifies behavior, not soundtrack production quality.
items.next: Audit every future cue against mixer levels and density limits.

items.title: A polished score with quiet space
items.acceptance: Original procedural music exists. It should develop across exploration, work and celebration without intrusive repetition or competing compositions.
items.next: Compose longer arrangements, improve instruments and review 20 minutes of listening.

items.title: Spatial Foley and ambience
items.acceptance: Distance and direction should match sources. Tires, motors and crowds must not mask essential cues; repetitive notification bursts must stay bounded.
items.next: Add source-based emitters, useful occlusion and measured mix headroom.

items.title: Dialogue and captions
items.acceptance: Written dialogue is not voice acting. Any recorded speech needs captions, a separate voice level and no audio-only essential information.
items.next: Decide licensed voice production or text-only presentation; add captions and voice bus before speech.

items.title: Unified art bible and approved reference shots
items.acceptance: Agree on palette, material response, scale and identity across buildings, hero, vehicles and nature. Compare actual gameplay, never concept images passed off as builds.
items.next: Create measured reference sheets and approved before/after captures.

items.title: Stable lighting and reflections
items.acceptance: No camera-driven sun rotation, blown highlights, flickering depth or shimmering shadows. Tone mapping and quality presets retain intended appearance.
items.next: Coastal Atmosphere adds user-selected daylight, golden hour, rain, after-rain and blue-hour presets with wet-road ripples, leaf light/wind and facade glow. Validate actual shaders and real hardware; live scene reflections, dynamic day/night, interiors and art approval remain open.

items.title: Time of day and weather with purpose
items.acceptance: User-selected daylight, golden-hour, after-rain, rainy and blue-hour visual presets are implemented. A simulated clock, automatically changing weather and weather-driven gameplay remain future work. Preserve readability and real-device frame targets.
items.next: Coastal Atmosphere adds user-selected daylight, golden hour, rain, after-rain and blue-hour presets with wet-road ripples, leaf light/wind and facade glow. Validate actual shaders and real hardware; live scene reflections, dynamic day/night, interiors and art approval remain open.

items.title: Controller-complete gameplay and menus
items.acceptance: Every feature including errors, confirmations, story, checklist and settings must be reachable and dismissible without a mouse after browser audio unlock. No gameplay input behind dialogs.
items.next: Run physical Xbox tests including disconnect, reconnect and multiple pads.

items.title: Remapping and input alternatives
items.acceptance: Support per-action keyboard/gamepad remapping, adjustable dead zones, hold/toggle alternatives and conflict-safe defaults. Essential actions need touch equivalents.
items.next: Build an input-action layer rather than more hard-coded mappings.

items.title: Readable and comfortable presentation
items.acceptance: Text scales without clipping; objectives are not color-only; speed effects can be reduced; long panels scroll by controller. Screen narration is not implemented.
items.next: Audit contrast, captions, text scaling, reduced motion and screen-reader access.

items.title: Automated model and controller evidence
items.acceptance: Coastal Atmosphere has 111 passing model/shader/save tests, 22 shader/UI checks, 14 retained-game controller checks and 12 Homecoming checks. Shader logs and actual screenshots are retained. Software WebGL does not certify physical hardware performance.
items.next: Keep physical-controller/GPU sign-off and extended soak testing open.

items.title: Physical hardware matrix
items.acceptance: Record Windows Chrome/Edge with Xbox USB and Bluetooth plus low-power and touch devices. Include sustained speed, menus, saves and audio.
items.next: Fill production/hardware-matrix.md with actual measured sessions.

items.title: Context loss and asset-failure recovery
items.acceptance: Graphics loss pauses safely and recovers with saves retained. Missing art falls back explicitly. New plaza and audio must survive the same path.
items.next: Add injected context loss, storage failures and missing-texture tests.

items.title: Extended soak and memory gate
items.acceptance: A 30-minute multi-district session has no uncaught exceptions, runaway voices, increasing geometry counts or stuck inputs. Compare a second lap.
items.next: Automate route-driven soak and record a real-device review.

items.title: Publish real source, not an unmerged candidate
items.acceptance: v0.7 is on master with a successful Pages deployment. Every next release preserves concurrent games, records a commit and checks live modules.
items.next: Apply this definition to v0.8 with a fresh release receipt.

items.title: A repeatable release gate
items.acceptance: Run model, browser, asset, visual and live checks before completion. Archive evidence, support reversible rollback and never force-push over sibling games.
items.next: Consolidate one-off workflows into a scoped release pipeline.

items.title: Licensed and reproducible assets
items.acceptance: The existing CC0 register retains sources and hashes. Every new model, texture, sound and voice needs provenance and redistribution rights.
items.next: Audit new assets, credits and reproduction for every milestone.

items.title: Evidence-based quality approval
items.acceptance: Do not call the game AAA because a checklist exists or a counter is large. All P0 gates, critical defects, approved art/play and actual hardware results must be resolved.
items.next: Close prerequisite gates and obtain explicit user quality approval.

items.title: Coastal Atmosphere shader pack
items.acceptance: All five visual presets compile on pinned r177; controller settings persist; off/reduced-motion/low modes work; wet shaders are stable around the planet; no physics changes or unbounded rain allocation. Record actual browser and shader results, not a concept mockup.
items.next: Automated shader/UI/recovery criteria passed. Obtain real-device timing and human visual approval; do not treat this shader check as AAA certification.

sources.title: WebGL best practices / Mozilla MDN
sources.use: Batching, bounded resources, avoiding synchronous stalls and cleanup. Numerical frame targets here are our project targets, not MDN requirements.
